scope: Four workout B shoulder/trapezius source sheets; visual illustration pilot, not professional biomechanics validation.
phase: lifting only; mirror for controlled return

machine-shoulder-press.observed: Handles rise from shoulder level toward overhead; torso/pelvis/feet stay supported. Two lever arms remain attached, visible loaded stack rises. No disappearing fixed post, added limb or obvious internal curve reversal identified.
machine-shoulder-press.watch: Inspect complete lever contours and hand/handle connections in interpolated frames.

dumbbell-lateral-raise.observed: Both arms rise from thighs to shoulder height with small elbow bend, little shoulder shrugging and no visible knee drive. Dumbbell count and shape retained, feet planted.
dumbbell-lateral-raise.watch: Inspect both wrists and dumbbells around middle/upper positions. Existing text supplies isometric top hold; sheet depicts dynamic lifting only.

cable-front-raise.observed: Bar rises in front from thighs toward shoulder height, elbows keep small bend, body upright. Low pulley behind, taut line to central bar attachment; stack rises without plate count change.
cable-front-raise.watch: Line is partly hidden by legs; ensure interpolated cable does not detach or become doubled at lower legs.

dumbbell-shrug.observed: Vertical shoulder elevation toward ears, elbows kept nearly straight, dumbbells rise at sides, no circular shoulder motion or obvious curl. Head-to-knees framing makes short range legible.
dumbbell-shrug.watch: Mild generated waist/head drift is present; avoid registering on moving shoulders/dumbbells. Head is intended fixed. Consider linear phase easing for small range; inspect quantified GIF count without adding noise.
